name: Primary Melanocytic Tumor of the Central Nervous System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on histopathology and exclusion

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of melanocytic tumor cells within CNS tissue
MRI or CT evidence of a melanocytic lesion localized to CNS without evidence of extracranial primary melanoma
Exclusion of systemic melanoma or other primary melanocytic tumors outside CNS
Positive immunohistochemical staining for melanocytic markers (e.g., HMB-45, Melan-A, S-100)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus imaging evidence localized to CNS and exclusion of extracranial primary melanoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary approach including neuroimaging, histopathology, and systemic evaluation to exclude metastatic melanoma.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits corresponding to tumor location
Seizures originating from affected CNS region
searchTerms: epileptic fits linked to CNS lesion

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment or altered mental status
Visual disturbances due to tumor involvement of optic pathways
searchTerms: vision problems from optic nerve tumor
blurred or lost vision due to tumor
visual changes from optic pathway involvement
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

occasional.symptomName: Neck stiffness or meningeal irritation signs

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord compression symptoms if tumor involves spinal meninges
searchTerms: spinal nerve symptoms from tumor meninges
nerve problems due to spinal tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic or pituitary involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain gland damage
endocrine imbalance due to brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Fever of unknown origin related to tumor necrosis

laboratory: CSF analysis may show elevated protein and presence of melanocytic cells
imaging: MRI shows hyperintense lesions on T1-weighted images due to melanin content
Contrast enhancement of lesion on MRI
CT may show hyperdense lesions with possible calcifications
genetic: Mutations in GNAQ and GNA11 genes reported in some cases
Absence of BRAF mutations typical of cutaneous melanoma
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, and S-100 protein
Histopathology shows melanin pigment and melanocytic tumor cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of known primary cutaneous or mucosal melanoma
Originates from meninges with meningioma histology
Typically lacks melanocytic markers like HMB-45

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Focal neurological deficits progressing over days to weeks
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System. 5th edition. IARC; 2021.
Kusters-Vandevelde HVN, et al. Primary melanocytic tumors of the CNS: a review. Acta Neuropathol. 2010.
Orphanet: Primary melanocytic tumor of the central nervous system. ORPHA:252028.
